title: Deterministic Universal Logical Gates for Finite-Energy GKP Qubits in Trapped Neutral Atoms
authors: Alok Kumar, Aaron N. Raja, Diksha Thapliyal, Ishitwa Kumar Das, Ajay Wasan1
abstract: We present a universal logical gate set for finite-energy Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) qubits encoded in the harmonic motional states of trapped neutral atoms. Internal electronic states serve as ancilla for implementing state-dependent conditional displacements in phase space, enabling arbitrary single-qubit phase gates. A Transient Rydberg excitation-mediated atomic dipole-dipole interaction enables a controlled-Z gate without invoking the blockade mechanism. The gates operate under magic-trapping conditions, allowing continuous trapping throughout the gate sequence, thereby preserving the motional encoding without intermediate measurement or feedforward. We assess the experimental feasibility of the proposed protocols using neutral $^{88}\mathrm{Sr}$ atoms and obtain average gate fidelities of $0.986$ for single-qubit phase gates and $0.985$ for the controlled-Z gate at a finite squeezing parameter of $Δ=0.25$ (12 dB of squeezing), increasing to $0.997$ and $0.995$ respectively as $Δ$ reaches $0.1$. These results provide a route toward universal, measurement-free logical control of motional GKP qubits in neutral-atom architectures.
summary: This paper presents a comprehensive protocol for implementing universal quantum gates on GKP qubits encoded in the motional states of trapped neutral atoms. By leveraging magic trapping and Rydberg interactions, the authors achieve high-fidelity, measurement-free logical control. This work provides a significant pathway toward scalable quantum computation using neutral-atom platforms.
main_problem: To develop and assess a universal, deterministic logical gate set for Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) qubits encoded in the motional states of trapped neutral atoms.
main_result: The authors propose a measurement-free scheme achieving high gate fidelities (e.g., >0.98) for single-qubit phase gates and controlled-Z gates, demonstrating viable logical control.
method: The gates are implemented using a combination of free harmonic evolution, ancilla-mediated conditional displacements in phase space, and transient Rydberg-mediated dipole-dipole interactions.
model_or_system: The system uses trapped neutral atoms (e.g., $^{88}	ext{Sr}$) where the motional states encode the GKP qubits. The protocol utilizes internal electronic states as ancillas and relies on magic trapping conditions to maintain the motional encoding throughout the gate sequence.
key_observables: Average gate fidelities ($ ar{F}$ and $F_{cz}$), which are measured as a function of the finite squeezing parameter $\Delta$.
important_parameters: Squeezing parameter ($\Delta$), which controls the finite-energy approximation; the Rydberg interaction strength ($C_6$).
main_assumptions: The protocol assumes continuous trapping (magic trapping) and relies on finite-energy approximations of the GKP code, with fidelity limited by residual quadratic interactions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the ideal versus finite-energy GKP states, the three-stage architecture for the phase gate, and plots showing gate fidelities improving as the squeezing parameter $\Delta$ decreases.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the finite GKP code, detailing the implementation of single-qubit gates via free evolution and conditional displacements, and finally implementing the two-qubit CZ gate using Rydberg interactions.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the physical realization of fault-tolerant quantum computation using neutral atoms, providing concrete, high-fidelity protocols for logical operations on continuous variable qubits.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Illustration of the ideal and finite-energy logical GKP basis states in the position quadrature. Ideal codewords consist of infinitely sharp peaks, while finite-energy codewords exhibit Gaussian-broadened peaks modulated by an overall Gaussian envelope whose width is determined by the squeezing parameter ∆.

FIG. 2. Gate architecture for logical phase gate. Composite displacement operation ˆD(θ, ζ) together with single- qubit rotations on the ancilla, realize a three-stage protocol consisting of ancilla–motional entanglement in leftmost panel, phase generation via a closed trajectory in phase space in central panel, and ancilla-motional disentanglement in rightmost panel. At the end of the sequence, the ancilla returns to its initial state while the motional GKP qubit acquires the target logical phase.

FIG. 3. Application duration t (µs) of the operator ˆU(t) as a function of the target logical phase ϕ. The required pulse duration of the tuned-out laser increases with the magnitude of the target logical phase.

FIG. 4. Schematic of the proposed neutral-atom architecture for implementing logical gates on motional GKP qubits. Two parallel optical lattice planes are separated by a distance R0, with each lattice site sparsely containing 88Sr atoms. The logical qubit is encoded in the axial motional mode of the atom, while the ancilla is encoded in the internal states |0⟩, |1⟩, and the Rydberg state |r⟩. For the controlled-Z gate, the two interacting atoms occupy the same (x, y) position in their respective lattice planes, so that their separation is along the z direction.

FIG. 5. The discrete points show the atomic separa- tion R0 required for the CZ gate for Rydberg interac- tion duration t. The corresponding separations lie well outside the blockade regime, consistent with the weak- interaction regime employed in the protocol.
